params.body:
Removing a vehicle did two things in a row: first withdraw the advert from Nederland Mobiel, then ring the webhook receivers. The withdrawal speaks over raw cURL, and until 20 September 2026 that call carried `CURLOPT_TIMEOUT => 0`, which means wait forever. A partner that did not answer held the request until PHP killed it, and a request that ends that way never reaches the line below. So the receivers were never told the car was gone, and because an aborted request is not an exception, nothing was recorded anywhere: no Nightwatch issue, and `last_nederland_mobiel_response` still held the successful answer from listing the car. `sold()` had the same order and the same trap.

## What was measured

On production, 28 September 2026:

- Between 16 and 21 September, **198 removals entered `VehiclePublisher::removed` and 164 came out**. The other 34 end in the log on `publisher->removed start` with nothing after it.
- Of the **122 portal vehicles removed since `webhook_deliveries` started recording** (15 September 20:43), **30 have no delivery at all**.
- The split is total: **all 30 were on Nederland Mobiel, and none of the 92 that did get a delivery were**. No overlap in either direction.
- Among the 30 is the black Opel Mokka of Garage Baert (vehicle 22441), which disappeared here on 16 September at 15:05 and was still on AS24 afterwards. That is the car the investigation started from.

An earlier count put this at 59 missing since 1 September. That count reached back further than the table: `webhook_deliveries` only exists since 15 September, so a vehicle removed before that cannot have a row even when the message did leave. A missing row is only evidence from the moment the table started writing.

## The fix

The ring goes first and the withdrawal after, in both `removed()` and `sold()`. That ordering is the actual repair, because a time limit that kills the request cannot be caught by anything: queueing a job is a row and costs nothing, so the message survives whatever happens at the third party afterwards. That a vehicle can leave the partner is a promise (R S2-10.4); that the advert is gone at a second party is not one that outranks it.

Underneath sits a net: the withdrawal moved into `withdrawQuietly()`, which catches `\Throwable` and reports it. `listOnNederlandMobiel` got exactly that guard on 15 September 2026 after a partner's throw broke a dealer's save; the withdrawal never got it, while it speaks to the same party over the same wire.

Two tests pin it, and both fail on the old order:

- `VehiclePublisherTest::test_a_partner_that_breaks_does_not_swallow_the_delete` — covers a throw, which a `catch` alone would also have handled.
- `VehiclePublisherTest::test_the_bell_rings_before_the_partner_is_spoken_to` — covers the ordering, which is the half that a `catch` cannot give.

## Not in here

The 30 vehicles are gone here and may still sit at a portal. Putting that right reaches into other companies' listings and should not ride along as a side effect; it is filed as an open point (`2026-09-28-de-dertig-wagens-staan-mogelijk-nog-bij-een-portaal`) for a decision.

One theory was investigated and refuted along the way, and stays closed: that a save without a signed-in user reaches nobody. The observer passes `$force = true` and the vehicle's owner decides, which `VehiclePublishingTest::test_force_takes_the_dealer_from_the_vehicle_instead_of_the_session` pins. The guard that did matter sits a level above that, in `VehicleObserver::deleted`, and turned out not to be a guard problem at all but an ordering one.

Replaces #839, which was opened while #838 was still in flight. The gateway pushes a snapshot rather than merging, so that branch carried the finding file as an add and conflicted the moment #838 brought its own copy into main. This is the same commit rebased onto main, where it applies cleanly.
params.title: The bell rings before the partner is spoken to
